pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
The Story

It is the morning of the Clown Club parade, and THE CHEZ is meant to lead it. Overnight, Gwinn buried Doc Leo's toolbox in the yard and tipped the Clown Club's instrument trunk in through the car's door window. Now THE CHEZ honks like a kazoo and rattles like a tambourine.

No wrenches? No problem. Doc Leo gives the car a tune-up by ear. He does his shrinking trick and climbs inside, and Sir Reginald III, his rubber chicken, does the fiddly bits: he fits where Doc Leo can't. Teddy rides along in the front passenger seat.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TUNEUP and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music and the notes; without one, the PC speaker plays the notes.

Pick Play from the menu. Before each level, Doc Leo taps his hat and pulls out the tool for the job, and a cutaway of THE CHEZ shows what is tuned so far. Then he and Sir Reginald III talk it over. Press a key to skip ahead.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Up hops; Q and E hop left and right. On a plug wire, Up climbs and Down climbs down. Space reaches up: hold it under a crank to turn it, or tap it to play a key. In Oil's Well, Z X C V B squirt the oil can. F2 shows what you have, F5 saves and F6 loads.

pages.head: Doc Leo and Sir Reginald III
pages.html:
Doc Leo and Sir Reginald III

Doc Leo is the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club: a chewed-up gray fedora with pins in its band, his own face paint, wire glasses, a patched navy corduroy jacket and red sneakers, and today a red shop rag in his pocket. He has an excellent ear.

Sir Reginald III is a rubber chicken of very good family. He does the repairs, tightens terminals with his beak and corrects Doc Leo's puns. Bump into him all you like; he is at work and does not mind.

A spark doesn't hurt Doc Leo; it frizzes his hair and costs a little energy. Energy comes back as you play: each note of the first key in The Timing Beat gives a little.

pages.head: The Engine Bay
pages.html:
The Engine Bay

1. Jump Start

The battery is flat. Find the red clamp on the shelf and the black clamp under the workbench: each opens its own terminal. Then stand under the crank and hold Space until the gauge is full.

2. Spark Plucks

The spark plugs are harp strings. Climb each wire and pluck its plug. Sparks run up the wires in the firing order, first, third, fourth, second: wait for yours to pass, then climb.

3. The Timing Beat

Notes drop down four glass pipes onto four keys. Stand under a key and tap Space as its note lands; right on the beat scores best. Three verses: a straight one, a syncopated one with a pipe that splits in two and one that takes the long way round, and a quick one with a pipe that crosses over the others. Each verse's gate opens when the meter at the top is full and you have played enough notes.

4. Oil's Well

Squeaks pace the five lines of a staff over Doc Leo's head. Z squirts oil along the bottom line, B the top. An oiled Squeak turns into a calm note that floats home to you. More Squeaks come out of the clef end as you go; bring every note home and the gate opens.

pages.head: Credits and Registering
pages.html:
Credits and Registering

Tune-Up, version 2.0, November 1994. Design, art, music and programming by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic's AI model), made in code for Game-Maker: Sandbox Edition. Built with GAME-MAKER 3.0 by Recreational Software Designs.

Starring Doc Leo as the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club, Sir Reginald III as himself, Teddy and Gwinn. Doc Leo's poses follow the ones drawn for CERTIFIED RAT TICKLER. The songs are played on the music editor's instrument presets. No wrenches were harmed. Gwinn would like that on the record.

This is shareware

Copy it for your friends and upload it to your favorite BBS. If you enjoy it, please register for $15 with Sandbox Software, Dept. HONK-ZOO, P.O. Box 000 (a made-up address: please don't mail anything). Registered players get a cutaway poster of THE CHEZ, and our thanks.
